# [L3 — The trend depends on the start year](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year")

*Generated by `scripts/pages/hypodraft_l3.py` from the draft as committed at `c601feb`. Counts of files held in this repository are read live. Counts that session made from external sources or from one-off runs are quotations of that commit - what the draft reported, shown as such, not re-derived by the build.*


*Test draft. Status: procedure specified and run once on bed oxygen; numbers below are that run, not a literature quote.*

## The observable consequence, stated so it can fail

[L3](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year") has a weak reading and a strong reading, and only the strong one is a claim about the sea.

**Weak:** *a slope fitted to a Danish series changes when you move the cut.* This is true of every noisy series ever fitted and is not worth testing — see the null below, which produces it [100](../SOURCES.md#F-3cb37b0769)% of the time from nothing.

**Strong:** *the window-dependence exceeds what a single constant rate plus the series' own autocorrelated noise would produce* — i.e. the record contains genuinely different eras, so "the trend" is not a well-defined quantity and reporting one number is a category error.

**Falsified if:** over the full space of admissible windows, the spread of fitted slopes, and the fraction of them that are positive, both fall inside the interval generated by simulating one constant slope with matched `AR(1)` noise. Then the window-dependence is noise around a single rate, the number is estimable, and [L3](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year")'s strong reading is not established for this variable.

**Supported if:** the observed surface is more dispersed, or its sign-share further from a single-trend expectation, than that simulation allows.

## Data, counted

`docs/data/areas/stations_series.{json,bin}` — [679,422](../SOURCES.md#F-b61d7944ec) station-months (verified: `sum(n)` over the [9](../SOURCES.md#F-81bea72caf) variables; `stations_series.bin` is [5,435,376](../SOURCES.md#F-91ec567fa1) bytes, exactly the declared layout), [1,415](../SOURCES.md#F-fff0060a3d) stations, month index [0](../SOURCES.md#F-e8bd5c9267)–[560](../SOURCES.md#F-03128e8f04) = 1980-[01](../SOURCES.md#F-1f20b582e3) to 2026-[09](../SOURCES.md#F-1395c72b82).

Variable used: **`oxy_bed`**, near-bed oxygen in mg/l, **[76,980](../SOURCES.md#F-a95c664ddf)** rows. Dropped **[472](../SOURCES.md#F-5418c43357)** as impossible ([432](../SOURCES.md#F-a58fb96f52) at ≤ [0](../SOURCES.md#F-bb43d7dc56) mg/l, [40](../SOURCES.md#F-9e053722ff) above [20](../SOURCES.md#F-46d89197fe) mg/l; the raw range is −[9.93](../SOURCES.md#F-faa4c72b1c) to [281.6](../SOURCES.md#F-6d53395d7a)) — **error class 1, value error**. Kept **[76,508](../SOURCES.md#F-b7b085c4ad)** rows on **[1,325](../SOURCES.md#F-250419bdd3)** stations.

Two further error classes are structural and are not fixed, only declared. The archive is already a **monthly median per station** — **class 3, aggregation**: within-month spread and the diel oxygen cycle are gone before I see the file, and there is **no time-of-day column anywhere** (**class 6, absent dimension**). Both inflate the year-to-year residual; the null below is matched to the residual actually observed, so they widen the null rather than being smuggled into the signal. The saturation cross-check uses `oxysat_bed`, which is computed from oxygen, temperature and salinity — **class 7, model-as-datum** — and is reported as a robustness check only.

## The constraint, and therefore the null

Constraint imposed: annual index years **1989–2025** ([37](../SOURCES.md#F-5d9ab391a4) years; before 1989 fewer than [200](../SOURCES.md#F-5ae7600a75) stations report per year, 2026 is a part-year of [819](../SOURCES.md#F-25b3e5351d) rows), windows of **≥ [10](../SOURCES.md#F-11b46510b6) years**, giving **[406](../SOURCES.md#F-d86478ae99) admissible windows**. Index = two-way fixed effects (station + calendar month, alternating demeaning to convergence), then the annual mean of residuals. Station effects absorb level differences, so composition change in *levels* cannot drive the index.

**The null is not "zero sensitivity".** For each station set I estimate ρ and σ from the detrended index, then simulate [4,000](../SOURCES.md#F-d1cc0c6816) `AR(1)` series of the same length and compute the same [406](../SOURCES.md#F-90419bcd6b)-window surface. Two nulls:

- **`H0`, no trend at all.** Sign-flipping windows occur in **[100.0](../SOURCES.md#F-4d2ab193b4)%** of simulations, in every station set. Median slope range [0.104](../SOURCES.md#F-9e0aad9990) mg/l/yr (pooled). *A sign flip carries no information whatsoever.*
- **`H1`, one constant slope equal to the fitted full-window slope, plus matched noise.** This is the null that [L3](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year")'s strong reading must beat.

Slopes in mg/l/yr. Fitted slopes run from **−[0.054](../SOURCES.md#F-1eda3a6373) to +[0.084](../SOURCES.md#F-f0fc9a329b)** (core set) — a [15](../SOURCES.md#F-c4935a4440)-fold range crossing zero. With the end fixed at 2025 every start year gives a negative slope (−[0.0085](../SOURCES.md#F-849a2fdf88) at 1989, −[0.054](../SOURCES.md#F-d95a924ada) at 2016); with the start fixed at 1989 the slope is **+[0.084](../SOURCES.md#F-a3b190f7bd)** ending 1998 and **−[0.0085](../SOURCES.md#F-e4ac3fd735)** ending 2025. **The sign is set by the end year, not the start year.**

**Every dispersion statistic is consistent with `H1`.** P(`H1` range ≥ observed) is [0.36](../SOURCES.md#F-c066983933)–[0.44](../SOURCES.md#F-7d875c494a) everywhere: one constant rate plus this series' own autocorrelation reproduces the whole surface.

## The two confounds

**Composition.** The summer-peaked share of `oxy_bed` station-months falls from [0.126](../SOURCES.md#F-7978ffad87) (1989–1994) to [0.035](../SOURCES.md#F-cc0244e4a0) (2015–2019) — the compositional shift is real and large in this variable. It is handled by re-running on a fixed [186](../SOURCES.md#F-b30f985340)-station core panel and on the [427](../SOURCES.md#F-6d17a82dae) year-round stations separately; both give the same answer, and the core panel gives a *stronger* directional signal, not a weaker one. My Rayleigh classification ([426](../SOURCES.md#F-c02d79aa56) summer / [427](../SOURCES.md#F-b6f811b838) year-round) is computed on `oxy_bed` rows only and does not reproduce the project's [293](../SOURCES.md#F-57ba3c93b9) / [481](../SOURCES.md#F-28994250b3) — treat the split as re-derived, not inherited.

**Thermometer.** Repeating on `oxysat_bed` ([64,493](../SOURCES.md#F-1f76a99b02) rows, [449](../SOURCES.md#F-c35745c5d1) dropped): the fraction of positive windows rises from [0.11](../SOURCES.md#F-f7e722331c)–[0.15](../SOURCES.md#F-a34f2db147) to **[0.28](../SOURCES.md#F-8dd461670d)–[0.30](../SOURCES.md#F-5997d01395)**, and the full-window slope is −[0.015](../SOURCES.md#F-e4a316a543) %sat/yr. Moving from a concentration to a saturation ruler roughly doubles the sign ambiguity. Consistent with part of the mg/l decline being solubility, not oxygen supply. Not separated here.

## What this licenses

Licensed: for near-bed oxygen in this archive, **[L3](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year")'s strong reading is not established**. The window-dependence is fully reproduced by one constant slope with matched autocorrelation, and the interesting asymmetry is the opposite of [L3](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year")'s framing — start year barely matters, end year decides the sign.

Not licensed: nothing about chlorophyll, nutrient loading, or the modelled reference condition, which is where [L3](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year")'s stake actually lies ([L1](../HYPOTHESES.md "The reference condition never existed"), [L2](../HYPOTHESES.md "The reference is a model output treated as a fact")). Nothing about pre-1980, which is the era [L3](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year") is really about — this archive starts at 1980, after the loading peak, so it cannot test "a trend measured from a peak". Nothing causal. And a negative here does not license reporting a single slope: the fitted rate still ranges −[0.054](../SOURCES.md#F-22f71bc726) to +[0.084](../SOURCES.md#F-4cde565b95), so any published number needs its window and its `H1` interval printed beside it.
